summary: Updated the Nestora firebombing record after Greek court reporters confirmed that all four defendants gave supplemental statements by October 23 and remained in pretrial detention at that point. The update distinguishes the alleged roles, records one defendant’s denial, and leaves the pending assessment unchanged.

Updated the Prairieland record with the June and July federal sentences and the pending Fifth Circuit appeals. The update distinguishes the defendant-specific convictions and sentences from the executive branch's broader Antifa framing, records the defense dispute, and preserves the finding that the case establishes a local cell rather than a national command structure.

Updated the Trump-attempts record after a November 12 superseding indictment added a D.C. act-of-terrorism-while-armed count against Cole Tomas Allen. The update records the new statutory allegation, his existing not-guilty pleas, the absence of a plea to the new count as of November 13, and the September 2027 trial schedule. It preserves the presumption of innocence and does not extend the charge into proof of a common far-left ideology or organization across the three incidents.

Updated the Direct Action Minnesota record with the October 22 superseding indictment and the October 7 release-conditions order. The current charging instrument retains 15 defendants and eight counts while distinguishing the group-wide conspiracy allegation from defendant-specific counts; the judicial order relaxed restrictions for ten defendants without deciding guilt. The assessment remains unchanged and all charges remain unadjudicated.

Added the May 2026 U.S. Counterterrorism Strategy to the administration-policy record because it formally makes violent left-wing extremists, including anarchists and anti-fascists, a national counterterrorism priority. The record treats the strategy as official policy and threat framing, not proof of particular organizational ties or crimes.

Updated the Quentin Deranque record after one murder defendant was released under judicial supervision and the prosecutor sought immediate review, and updated the Kyle Wagner record after the Supreme Court denied certiorari in his pretrial-detention appeal. Neither development decides guilt or changes the assessments.

Updated the Charlie Kirk case after the court scheduled jury selection for June 21, 2028, and reserved 105 court days for trial; the procedural update does not change the assessment or the presumption of innocence.

Updated the Mangione record after the defense filed its October 30 reply seeking dismissal of the remaining New York murder and weapons charges under state double-jeopardy law; the motion remains undecided and the assessment is unchanged.

Updated the Quentin Deranque record after anti-terrorism police questioned Jeune Garde cofounder and LFI lawmaker Raphaël Arnault in a voluntary interview, while making explicit that reporting did not identify him as charged and that questioning does not establish command or culpability.

Updated the Charlie Kirk case after the October 23 scheduling hearing ended without a trial date and the court set a November 9 hearing to rule on the competing proposed timelines; the assessment and dimensional findings remain unchanged.

Updated the Kyle Wagner record after the Supreme Court denied his application to stay the Sixth Circuit mandate, while preserving the distinction between pretrial detention and adjudication of the pending charges.
Updated the Mangione record after Manhattan prosecutors filed their opposition to the pending state double-jeopardy dismissal motion; the assessment and dimensional findings remain unchanged.

Added dimensional assessments, per-record review dates, structured source provenance, explicit sampling limits, a public corrections log, validation gates, and daily monitoring. Updated active cases and policy actions through October 7, 2026.
Published the 30-claim Rubio speech audit, 13-case ANTIFA attribution ledger, and five-record policy-framing audit.
